sop_nsi_001.title: No Sweat Intro (NSI) — Sales Floor SOP
sop_nsi_001.summary: Full step-by-step process for conducting a No Sweat Intro from greeting through sign-up.
steps: GREETING: Greet them by name at the door. Ask: 'Hey, what brings you in today?'
FIND THE DEEP WHY: Keep asking 'Why?' until you reach the real pain point. If they give a vague answer, follow up with another why. Keep digging until you hit something emotional and specific.
Share social proof: tell a story of a member with the same pain point and explain what changed for them.
If they ask what CrossFit is, explain: coaching-first facility, functional fitness, scalable to every person. Tie it back to their why. Emphasize they came here for a human coach, not amenities.
CONFIRM THE 10/10 (before the tour): State their goal back to them. Ask: 'If we got you [their goal] in the next 90 days, would that be a 10 out of 10 experience for you?'

If they say yes, move to the tour. If they say no, ask: 'What would make it a 10 out of 10? What would have you telling all your friends or staying here forever?' Repeat it back and confirm before moving on.

GYM TOUR: Walk through PT side, back alley (lockers, cubbies, bathrooms, showers), recovery equipment, water fountain, snacks, and group class floor. End with: 'Any questions about the space? Alright — let's go talk pricing.'
PRICING (Office): Set chairs turned toward the door — never block the exit. Open with: 'Based on what we talked about, here is what I recommend.' Choose the package based on their goal and schedule.
Pricing reference — PT: 30 min $55, 45 min $85, 60 min $105. CrossFit: 4x/mo $113, 8x/mo $215, 12x/mo $225, Unlimited $239. Bundle packages: round down to nearest $5 or $9.
Walk through the 90-day roadmap: Days 1-30 = on-ramp and form. Days 31-60 = add intensity and first InBody check-in. Days 61-90 = transition to regular schedule tracking toward goal.
Close with: 'How does that sound — are you ready to get started?'

OBJECTION — Spouse/Partner: Ask if they talked beforehand. Offer to step out so they can call right now. If they agree after the call, proceed. If no, schedule a callback with a specific date and time.

OBJECTION — Too expensive: Ask what price range would get them started. Scale down the package accordingly. If around $100, refer to CrossFit Drive. Re-close with: 'With all that said — what is stopping us from getting you signed up today?'

OBJECTION — Need to think about it: Ask how long it took from first looking you up to coming in. Reframe: 'You have already thought about it. Is it really about budget?' Anchor the value: 'You could go to Planet Fitness for $10 a month. You came here because you wanted a coach.' If they hold firm a second time, back off and schedule a follow-up.

OBJECTION — Did not expect it to be this much: If comparing to another CrossFit gym, explain cost of living and downtown rent difference. If they had no expectation, explain what it costs to pay a coach a sustainable wage.
SIGN-UP: Open Wodify and Lead Machine simultaneously. Have them fill in details while having a natural conversation — learn their job, friends, and hobbies to identify referral opportunities.
Add PT membership first. Bake the full bundle price into the PT line item and set CrossFit to $0.
Walk through PT agreement: initial next to price, initial confirming 24-hour cancellation policy, and promptness requirement. Have them sign and collect payment.
Schedule the first PT session before they leave. Try to keep them with the same coach every time.
Add CrossFit membership if applicable and have them sign the CrossFit waiver.
Close with: 'Is there anything else I can help you with? Can't wait to see you on [date]!'
POST SIGN-UP: Send New Athlete Alert to all coaches in Slack. Add to Athlete Check-In List, Affinity Sheet, and On-Ramp List. Mark account created and start date confirmed.

sop_communication_001.title: The 6 Steps to 10/10 Communication — Vegvisir
sop_communication_001.summary: 6 rules for coach communication: Personal service rule, proactive CALM framework, highest communication level, active listening, next date strategy, and nourishing sequences.
steps: RULE 1 — Personal Service: Know your clients' friends, family, where they work, and their hobbies. Connect every session back to their life and how it will be better. Ask them directly: 'How can I provide a 10 out of 10 experience for you?'

RULE 2 — Proactive Engagement (CALM): When something goes wrong, never go quiet. Use CALM — Clarity (explain what happened), Assurance (confirm you have it handled), Leadership (make a decision), Movement (tell them what's next). Own your mistakes, explain what you will do differently, and keep moving forward.

RULE 3 — Use the Highest Communication Level Available: In person is best, then video call, then phone call, then voice note, then text, then email. Email is the worst option. Never email what can be a call. If there is any issue or conflict, call immediately.

RULE 4 — Active Listening: Make consistent eye contact (focus on their left eye). Put your phone away. When they share a concern, reflect it back: 'I am sorry you feel that way — can you tell me more about what is contributing to this?' Ask questions to get more context. Be curious, not judgmental. Never assume malice — look for the simplest explanation.

RULE 5 — Next Date Strategy: Every conversation ends with the next one scheduled — a specific date and time, not 'let's catch up soon.' Say: 'I will see you at 4 PM on Tuesday.' This is one of the best things you can do to build deep relationships.

RULE 6 — Nourishing Sequences: A lead who said no today is a future client who is not ready yet. Go high frequency early, taper over time, never go to zero. A personal check-in text or call at 6 months converts leads that automation never will. Treat every person — member or not — with respect.

Go to the Coaches section.
Tap Schedule and select today's class, then tap the specific class you coached.
Tap WOD, then tap Results on the block you want to score.
Tap the athlete's name and enter their result.
For strength portions: always enter the weight lifted. If it is a max reps movement, enter total reps completed plus the weight used.

For metcons: enter every single scale used — even if there are 7 different movements with 7 different scales, enter all of them. Never just put Rx or Performance+. Athletes need to see exact weights and modifications so they can track their progress over time. Six months from now they need to know if they used a 20 lb or 25 lb dumbbell.

sop_prs_001.title: Looking Up PRs — Protocol
sop_prs_001.summary: Option 1: app.wodify.com > Reports > Personal > Standard Reports > Personal Records. Option 2: Wodify app > Leaderboard (look for stars).
steps: OPTION 1 (most detail): Go to app.wodify.com and log in with your coach/admin credentials. Go to Reports. Go to Personal, then Standard Reports, then Personal Records. Select Weightlifting or MetCon depending on what you are looking up. Type in the athlete's name to see their full PR list.
OPTION 2 (quick view): Open the Wodify app. Go to Leaderboard. Stars next to an athlete's name indicate PRs.

sop_kiosk_setup_001.title: Kiosk Setup for Class — Protocol
sop_kiosk_setup_001.summary: Orange iPad and black iPad: Safari > app.wodify.com > login > menu > Extensions > Kiosk Plus > Workout. Use orange iPad to sign athletes in.
steps: On the orange iPad and small black iPad: open Safari.
Go to app.wodify.com and log in using the gym credentials.
Tap the 3 lines (menu) in the top corner.
Scroll to the bottom and tap the square with an arrow icon — this is Extensions.
Select Kiosk Plus.
Tap Workout.
Open the Wodify app (find it in recently opened apps or on the first page of apps).
Use the orange iPad to sign athletes into class.

sop_music_volume_001.title: Music — Turning On & Volume Guidelines
sop_music_volume_001.summary: Open Sonos, pick approved playlist. Volume: 28 normal hours, 50-60 strength, 70-80 metcon. Pause and lock iPad when done.
steps: Open the Sonos app on the iPad.
Select an approved playlist.
Set the volume based on what is happening in the gym: Normal operating hours = 28. Strength portion = 50-60. MetCon = 70-80.
When you are done: pause the music and lock the iPad. Do not leave music running overnight.

sop_music_zones_001.title: Sonos — Different Music for PT vs Group Training
sop_music_zones_001.summary: Select a playlist, tap Play, choose which room (PT or Group), repeat for the other side. To play the same music in both rooms, select both.
steps: Open Sonos and tap the playlist you want for one side.
When you hit Play, a prompt will appear asking which area to play it in.
Select either Personal Training or Group Training — not both.
Go back and select a different playlist for the other side. Repeat the same steps, selecting the opposite room.
If you want the same music playing in both rooms: select a playlist and when prompted choose both rooms.

sop_ipad_charging_001.title: iPad Charging — Protocol
sop_ipad_charging_001.summary: Charge at benches under group class TV (USB-C and Lightning) or at front desk black box (left side). All iPads must be at 100% each morning. Leave plugged in overnight.
steps: Charging locations: benches underneath the front group class TV (USB-C and Lightning cables available). Front desk left side — black box with 1 Lightning and 1 USB-C cable. Watches can also be charged here.
All iPads must be at 100% charge at the start of each morning.
Leave all iPads plugged in to charge overnight — do not unplug them when you leave.

sop_fans_001.title: Fans — Operating Protocol
sop_fans_001.summary: Orange fan (group side): power button on, dial up, then dial all the way down and wait for full stop before powering off. Yellow fan (PT side): set dial first, push button to start and stop.
steps: ORANGE FAN (Group Training Side) — To turn ON: hit the power button, then turn the dial up to the desired speed.

ORANGE FAN — To turn OFF: turn the dial all the way down and wait for the fan to come to a complete stop. Only then hit the power button to turn it off. Do not hit the power button while the fan is still spinning.
YELLOW FAN (PT Side) — To turn ON: set the dial to your desired speed beforehand, then push the button to start it.
YELLOW FAN — To turn OFF: push the button again.

sop_lights_001.title: Gym Lights — Turning On Protocol
sop_lights_001.summary: Lights turn on automatically via motion sensors. If not, check both light switches by the front door are up. Then manually push both motion sensors.
steps: Lights should turn on automatically when you enter: PT side turns on when you walk in, group training side turns on when you walk past the 2nd squat rack.
If the lights do not turn on automatically, check that both light switches next to the front door are in the UP position.
If the switches are up but lights still are not on, manually activate the motion sensors.
Motion sensor 1: located by the orange fan control box on the group training side — push it in.
Motion sensor 2: located behind the sleds on the PT side — push it in.

sop_pos_001.title: Point of Sale — Protocol
sop_pos_001.summary: Use the POS iPad at the snack kiosk for self-checkout. If not working, log into app.wodify.com > Point of Sale and process manually.
steps: The point of sale iPad at the snack kiosk should be fully charged at the start of each day.
Normal checkout: athlete selects what they want, goes to cart, signs in, and pays with their card.
If the point of sale iPad is not working, log into app.wodify.com with your coach/admin credentials.
Go to Point of Sale. Add the item(s) the athlete is purchasing. Type in the athlete's name at checkout.
Charge to their default card on file unless they want to use a different payment method.

sop_247_membership_001.title: 24/7 Membership — Adding & Canceling
sop_247_membership_001.summary: Eligibility: 90+ days as member and coach confirms safety. Add in Wodify then set up Kisi access (vegvisircrossfit, Entry Door Access Group). Cancel by reversing the process.
steps: Before adding a 24/7 membership, confirm both eligibility requirements are met: the member has been with us for at least 90 days, and a coach has confirmed they are safe in class (they do not put themselves or others at risk).
Go to the athlete's profile in Wodify. Tap + Membership. Select 24/7 Membership.
Have them sign the membership agreement on the spot.
Go to web.kisi.io on a Vegvisir iPad or computer. Search the company name: vegvisircrossfit (one word). Log in — password is saved on the device.
Go to Users in the top left banner. Tap New User.
Enter their name and email. Select access group: Entry Door Access Group.
Set the start date to match their membership start date. Hit Save.
The athlete will receive an email from Kisi with instructions to set up access on their phone.
TO CANCEL: reverse the process — remove them from Kisi first (delete from Users in Kisi), then remove the 24/7 membership in Wodify.

sop_emergency_hold_001.title: Emergency Hold — When & How
sop_emergency_hold_001.summary: For members who cannot exercise at all (bedridden or doctor ordered no exercise). Place for 2 months with biweekly check-in texts. Standard holds require 30 days notice.
steps: Emergency holds are only for members who are completely unable to exercise — bedridden, or doctor has ordered no physical exercise. If neither applies, a standard hold requires 30 days notice.
Place the hold immediately for 2 months.
Go to their athlete profile in Lead Machine. Go to Messages.
Schedule a check-in text every 2 weeks at 8:30 AM on a Monday or Tuesday: 'Hey [Name], how is recovery going? Is there anything we can do to help at this time?'
Continue biweekly check-ins until the 2-month mark.
If they recover within 2 months, resume membership normally.
If they need longer than 2 months, handle case by case and continue biweekly check-ins.
If the hold reaches 3-5 months, scale back to monthly check-ins.
If the hold exceeds 6 months, cancel the membership and continue monthly check-in texts to stay in touch and leave the door open.

sop_fire_member_001.title: Firing a Member — Protocol
sop_fire_member_001.summary: Evaluate against humble/hungry/people-smart values. Escalate to GM/Owner. Schedule a sit-down, offer referral to CrossFit Drive, process refund, mark account Suspended.
steps: Evaluate the athlete: are they humble, hungry, and people-smart? In practice this means — are they listening to coaching cues? Are they being safe? Are they being respectful of other people's bodies, space, and emotions?
If they are checking all those boxes, no action needed.
If they are being repeatedly disrespectful, violent in any way, damaging property, or behaving in a way you would not tolerate in your own home — escalate immediately.
Bring it to the General Manager or Owner. Explain exactly what is happening. The Owner and GM make the final call.

If the decision is made to let them go, the Owner or GM sits down with the member and says: 'We are going to recommend that you find a different gym. You are not quite the right fit for us and we think you would be better served somewhere else. We have gone ahead and refunded your money. We do recommend CrossFit Drive down the street — they would be a great fit. If you would like, instead of a refund I can send that money over and pay for your first month there. It has been great having you and we wish you the best of luck.'
Add a note to their Wodify profile: Suspended.

sop_refunds_001.title: Refunds — Policy & Protocol
sop_refunds_001.summary: No refunds policy except: Texas 72-hour law (mandatory full refund within 72 hours of start) and gym negligence injuries (case by case). Process via Wodify Paid Invoices.
steps: The gym has a no refunds policy with two exceptions.

EXCEPTION 1 — Texas 72-Hour Law (mandatory): if a member requests a refund within 72 hours of their membership start date, issue a full refund. This is required by Texas law and there are no exceptions. Example: membership starts June 1, full refund must be honored through June 4.
EXCEPTION 2 — Gym Negligence Injury: if a member is severely injured due to our negligence, escalate to the Owner immediately. Refund and next steps will be determined case by case.
All other refund requests: no refund per gym policy.

TO PROCESS A PARTIAL REFUND (e.g. incorrect charge): go to the athlete's account in Wodify. Go to Invoices, then Paid Invoices. Click on the invoice in question. Click the invoice link and hit Refund Money. Type in the partial amount.
TO PROCESS A FULL REFUND: go to Paid Invoices. Click the Refund Money link next to the full invoice. Confirm — the full amount will be refunded.

sop_2on1_intro_001.title: 2-on-1 Free Intro PT Session — When to Offer
sop_2on1_intro_001.summary: Offer a free 2-on-1 PT session with a friend when a member has been with us 90+ days and has gotten their desired results. Clear with GM or Owner first.
steps: A free 2-on-1 intro PT session can be offered when a member has been with us for 90 or more days AND has gotten the results they came for.
Both conditions must be met — 90+ days and results achieved.
Clear it with the General Manager or Owner before offering.
Invite the member to bring a friend to join their next personal training session at no charge.
Treat the session as a full intro experience for the friend.

sop_friend_pt_001.title: Friend Joining a Personal Training Session
sop_friend_pt_001.summary: If friend wants to become a member: session is free. If visiting: charge 2-on-1 rate ($145 for 45 min) and invoice the difference. If they decline, find another way to get them in.
steps: If a PT member asks if their friend can join their session, first ask: is the friend interested in becoming a member?
If the friend wants to become a member: the session is free. Welcome them in and treat it as a full intro opportunity.

If the friend is just visiting (out of town or not interested in joining): offer the 2-on-1 rate. Say: 'It is a little cheaper for both of you and we do a bit more work — so the rate for two is $145 for a 45-minute session versus $85 for one.'
If they agree to the 2-on-1 rate: adjust their account and create an invoice for the difference only. Example: $145 minus $85 = $60 extra for that session.
If they do not want to pay the 2-on-1 rate: ask 'Is there a Bring a Friend day coming up? Let's find the best way to get them in.' If no good option exists, the friend cannot join that session.
Notify the General Manager if this situation comes up and you cannot resolve it cleanly.

sop_makeup_classes_001.title: Making Up Classes — Policy
sop_makeup_classes_001.summary: All sessions must be used within the month they start — no rollover. Members can make up missed sessions within the same month. Adjust membership tier if consistently underusing.
steps: All sessions must be used within the month they start. Unused sessions do not roll over to the next month — this is in the membership agreement.
If a member asks to make up sessions they missed within the same month, the answer is yes. They can double up sessions in a later week as long as they use all sessions before the month ends.
If a member is consistently not using all their sessions (e.g. has a 12x membership but only averaging 7), suggest dropping down to a lower tier such as 8x until they are ready to go back up.
Both CrossFit and PT memberships can be adjusted up or down month to month without changing contracts.

sop_friend_tryout_001.title: Friend Trying Out Vegvisir — Options
sop_friend_tryout_001.summary: Three options: Bring a Friend Day, Free Intro on website, or 2-on-1 PT session for loyal 90+ day members.
steps: OPTION 1 — Bring a Friend Day: check announcements for the next Bring a Friend Day and get the friend signed up for it.
OPTION 2 — Free Intro Consultation: direct the friend to vegvisircrossfit.com, have them go to Free Intro, and book a consultation.

OPTION 3 — 2-on-1 Intro PT Session (for strong, loyal members only): if the member has been around 90+ days and is someone the coaching staff genuinely knows and values, text a manager to let them know you're planning this. Offer the member a free 2-on-1 PT session with their friend. Ask what date works best. Confirm the date with the General Manager.

sop_no_dropins_001.title: No Free Drop-Ins — Policy & Explanation
sop_no_dropins_001.summary: Vegvisir does not offer free drop-ins. Redirect to Bring a Friend Day, Free Intro, or paid 2-on-1 PT.
steps: Vegvisir does not offer free drop-ins. If someone requests one, decline and redirect them.
Direct them to one of the options in the Friend Trying Out Vegvisir SOP.

If they ask why we do not offer free drop-ins, you can explain: bringing an inexperienced athlete into a group class pulls coaching attention away from paying members, which is not fair to them. We are professionals and our time has value. We want people here because they genuinely want to be part of what we offer — not because it was free.

sop_dropin_eligibility_001.title: Drop-Ins — Eligibility & Protocol
sop_dropin_eligibility_001.summary: Must be active CrossFit member for 6+ months. Verify home gym in Lead Machine Additional Info. Google unknown gyms. If not from a CrossFit gym, redirect to CrossFit Drive.
steps: To be eligible for a drop-in, the person must have been an active member at a CrossFit gym for 6 or more months leading up to the drop-in date.
Ask what their home gym is. Go to their Lead Machine profile and check Additional Info to see the home gym they listed.
If it says CrossFit [something] or [something] Athletics, Google the gym to confirm it is active and open with a real website. If confirmed, approve the drop-in.
If the gym name is unfamiliar, Google it. If it shows barbells, rigs, and looks like a CrossFit-style gym with an active website, approve the drop-in.
If the gym has fewer than 55 five-star Google reviews, do not approve or recommend it.

If the person does not have CrossFit experience: do not approve the drop-in. Ask what kind of gym they are looking for. Recommend CrossFit Drive (accepts people with CrossFit experience) or the nearest highly rated gym with 55+ five-star reviews. Be as kind as possible.

sop_hold_001.title: Membership Hold — Policy & Protocol
sop_hold_001.summary: Holds require 30 days notice and cannot exceed 6 months. Direct to vegvisircrossfit.com/hold. Process in Wodify under Membership > Options > Add Hold. Confirm via Lead Machine text.
steps: Holds require 30 days notice. If their entire reason for the hold falls within the next 30 days, no hold can be granted.

If only part of their absence extends beyond the 30-day window, only that portion can be put on hold. Example: trip is June 27 - July 14, request made June 1 — only July 1 through July 14 can be held.
If the hold would need to exceed 6 months, recommend they cancel and rejoin when they return.

If the hold cannot be granted, offer alternatives: drop-in reimbursement at another CrossFit gym (up to half their CrossFit membership value back as credit), travel programming via TrueCoach, travel workout packets, or help finding a local CrossFit affiliate.
If the hold qualifies: direct them to fill out the hold form at vegvisircrossfit.com/hold.
In Wodify: go to the athlete's profile, tap their name, go to Membership, then Options, then Add Hold. Enter the approved hold dates.

Send a confirmation text via Lead Machine. For travel: 'Hey [Name], your hold is in place. Thank you so much for being a member of Vegvisir CrossFit — we hope you have a wonderful trip!' For illness or injury: 'Hey [Name], your hold is in place. We hope you heal well — please let us know if there is anything we can do for you!'

sop_cancel_membership_001.title: Canceling a Membership — Protocol
sop_cancel_membership_001.summary: Cancellation accepted via form, email (vegvisircrossfit@gmail.com), or text (713-715-1440). PT: stop auto-renew at end of period. CrossFit: generate next membership, prorate, stop auto-renew. Confirm via Lead Machine.
steps: Valid cancellation requests must come through one of these channels: cancellation form on the website, email to vegvisircrossfit@gmail.com, or text to 713-715-1440.

FOR PERSONAL TRAINING MEMBERSHIPS: go to the athlete's account in Wodify. Go to Memberships and click the membership link. Go to Options and hit Stop Auto-Renew. Set the end date to when the current membership period ends. Deactivate the athlete's account on that date.
FOR CROSSFIT (GROUP CLASS) MEMBERSHIPS (30 days notice required): go to the athlete's account, open their current membership, go to Options, and click Generate Next Membership.

Open the newly generated membership (it will have a green checkmark). Go to Options and hit Stop Auto-Renew. Set the end date to the second month's end date. Example: billing date is the 15th and the request came in June 1 — membership ends August 30.

Calculate the prorated amount for the current billing period: take their membership rate divided by 30 to get the daily rate. Multiply the daily rate by the number of days remaining until their next billing date. Go to their invoice, click the invoice link, click the membership line item, and adjust the invoice payment to that prorated amount.

Send a confirmation text via Lead Machine: 'Hey [Name], we have received your cancellation and have processed it. We are so sorry to see you go! Your final payment will be [amount] on your usual billing date. You will be able to attend until 30 days from now. If you have any questions, please let us know — we hope to see you as much as possible before you go!'
If anything about the cancellation is unusual or does not fit this process, refer to the Unusual Cancellations SOP.

sop_hybrid_membership_001.title: Hybrid / On-Ramp Membership — Setup Protocol
sop_hybrid_membership_001.summary: Create PT membership first in Wodify (Customized, correct price, no auto-renew). Get waiver signed. Add CrossFit membership with On-Ramp payment plan ($0). Write VOID on CrossFit signature line. Book all appointments.
steps: Go to the athlete's account in Wodify. Go to New Membership, then Appointment Memberships.
Select the On-Ramp or 8 Personal Training Sessions (45 min) option.
Select CUSTOMIZED — not Quick Add. This is required.
Set the price to the agreed amount (e.g. $775). Set No Auto-Renew. Confirm the start date is correct. Hit Next.
If the athlete asks about the CrossFit portion, explain: 'We will add that right after this — we just need to get your payment info set up first.'
Have them sign the PT agreement and collect payment info as you would for any PT membership. Book their first PT session before they leave.
Go to Waivers and have the athlete sign the gym waiver.
Go to New Membership and select the CrossFit option that matches the package (e.g. 1x/4x CrossFit membership).
Set the start date to match the PT membership start date. Set the payment plan to On-Ramp — this will zero out the CrossFit cost to $0.
Hit Sign. Enter their initials. On the signature line, write VOID. Close it out.
Go to Appointments, hit New Appointment, select the correct date, time, and available coach. Book all upcoming PT sessions.
Have the athlete open their Welcome to Vegvisir CrossFit email so they can access their Wodify account and see both memberships in place.

sop_pt_membership_001.title: Personal Training Membership — Setup Protocol
sop_pt_membership_001.summary: Athlete account > + Membership > Appointment Memberships > Quick Add. Walk through PT agreement. Collect payment. Book first appointment.
steps: Go to the athlete's account in Wodify. Tap + Membership. Go to Appointment Memberships.
Select the agreed-upon membership — choose between solo or couples. Make sure it shows the price that was agreed upon.
If no price adjustments are needed, select Quick Add. Confirm the start date is correct.

Walk through the PT agreement with the athlete: have them initial next to the price. Have them initial confirming the 24-hour cancellation policy — sessions must be canceled at least 24 hours in advance. If it is a genuine emergency, they must notify us and can make up the session within 30 days. Also go over promptness — we cannot make up lost time if they are late.
Have them read and sign the PT waiver. Go over any concerns they have. For the full gym waiver, refer to the Waiver SOP.
Collect payment info. Ask whether they prefer payment today or on their start date — either is fine.
Ask if they would like to set up auto-renew. PT does not auto-renew by default.
Go to Appointments in Wodify and hit New Appointment. If unsure of coach availability, check the Availabilities tab in the Appointments section.
Book their first session, confirm the coach, and let the athlete know who they will be working with.

sop_new_member_account_001.title: Creating a New Member Account — Protocol
sop_new_member_account_001.summary: app.wodify.com > Athletes > New Athlete. Enter first name, last name, email, and phone. Save. Then proceed to appropriate membership SOP.
steps: Go to app.wodify.com and log in with your admin username and password.
Go to Athletes. Tap New Athlete in the top right.

Enter their first name, last name, email, and phone number. Pull this info from their Lead Machine profile or confirm directly with them. Always make sure you know their first name — it goes a long way in making them feel welcome.
Hit Save. Their account is now created.

Proceed to the appropriate membership SOP based on what they signed up for: PT only = Personal Training Membership SOP. PT + CrossFit = Hybrid/On-Ramp Membership SOP. 24/7 access = 24/7 Membership SOP.

sop_dropin_booking_001.title: Drop-In — Booking Protocol
sop_dropin_booking_001.summary: Drop-in fills out form via Lead Machine. Auto-message goes out. Verify CrossFit gym. Send Wodify class link. If not from CrossFit gym, redirect to CrossFit Drive.
steps: The drop-in fills out the drop-in form via Lead Machine. An automatic message goes out asking what time they would like to drop in.
Wait for their response.
Go to their Lead Machine profile and check Additional Info to verify they belong to a CrossFit gym. Refer to the Drop-Ins — Eligibility SOP for full criteria.
If they are eligible: go to vegvisircrossfit.wodify.com. Select the class time they requested. Copy the class link.
Send them the link with: 'Here is your link to drop into the [time] class! Once it is filled out you will be good to go. Is there anything else we can help with before your drop-in?'
Answer any questions they have and close with: 'Have a wonderful day — we cannot wait to train with you at Vegvisir!'
If they are not eligible: decline kindly. Direct them to CrossFit Drive (accepts people with CrossFit experience) or the nearest highly rated gym. Be as kind as possible.

sop_rings_001.title: Gymnastic Rings — Height Adjustment & Storage
sop_rings_001.summary: Push black clasp down to adjust height. Feed strap against the teeth. Tuck excess strap in containment strap. Test by putting weight on the ring.
steps: Find the black clasp on the strap of the ring you want to adjust.
Push the clasp down and move the strap up or down to the desired height.
Make sure the strap is fed against the teeth so it does not slide.
If you are unsure it is secured correctly: put some weight on the ring. If the ring starts to move, it is fed through the wrong way. Re-feed and try again.
After adjusting: fold up any excess strap and tuck it within the containment strap. Excess strap should never be left hanging or on the floor.

sop_rogue_rig_001.title: Rogue Rig — Adjusting Pull-Up Bars
sop_rogue_rig_001.summary: Requires owner approval. Tools: 15/16 socket, 1/2 drive wrench, 1 inch wrench. Flat washer on bolt head side, split lock washer + nut on open side. Adjustable pull-up bars need no approval.
steps: If you need to adjust an adjustable pull-up bar: no owner approval is needed — adjust freely.
If you need to adjust a standard pull-up bar height on the Rogue rig: this requires owner approval before doing anything. Do not proceed without it.
Once owner has approved: gather tools — 15/16 socket, 1/2 inch drive socket wrench, and large 1 inch wrench.
Unscrew the bolts using the socket wrench and 1 inch wrench.
Move the bar to the desired height.
Reinstall with the correct hardware: flat washer up against the bolt head on the bolt head side, and split lock washer plus nut on the open side.
Tighten securely.

sop_bike_maintenance_001.title: Bike Maintenance — Protocol
sop_bike_maintenance_001.summary: Bent cage bars: needle nose pliers. Belt wear: open housing with Phillips head, swap belt. Need parts? Notify Kidd or Rob.
steps: If any cage pedal bars are bent: use needle nose pliers to pull them back into shape.
If there is visible wear on the belt: open the belt housing using a Phillips head screwdriver. Keep track of all screws.
Loosen the old belt and remove it.
Install the new belt.
Reassemble and tighten all screws.
If you need replacement parts: notify Kidd (owner) or Rob (engagement coordinator) and they will get it ordered and fixed.

sop_rower_maintenance_001.title: Rower Maintenance — Scheduled Protocol
sop_rower_maintenance_001.summary: Every 6 months: open casing with Phillips head, remove damper side panel, blow out all debris with pressurized air or leaf blower, reassemble.
steps: Perform this maintenance every 6 months.
Use a Phillips head screwdriver to open the rower casing.
Remove the side panel that has the damper on it.
Use a pressurized air can or the leaf blower to blow out all dust, dirt, dog hair, and debris from inside.
Reassemble the casing and tighten all screws.

sop_barbell_maintenance_001.title: Barbell Maintenance — Full Protocol
sop_barbell_maintenance_001.summary: Tools from gray first aid cabinet top shelf: 30in box, 3 towels, snap lock pliers (blue handles), 3-in-1 oil. Disassemble, clean, oil with hands, reassemble in reverse. Leave flat 24 hours.
steps: Applies to men's barbells (Ohio symbol on end cap) and women's barbells (dog symbol on end cap) — same procedure for both.

Gather tools from the top shelf of the gray first aid cabinet: 30 inch plyo box (work surface), 3 regular gym towels, snap lock pliers (blue handles, gray square bottom, set to close), and 3-in-1 oil (white and red bottle with red cap).

DISASSEMBLY — lay parts on the box in the exact order you remove them: use snap lock pliers to remove the first O-ring. Tap out the coin (it blocks residue from entering). Remove the second O-ring. Remove the thin metal ring. Remove the two half-moon rings from the groove. Remove the thick ring. Slide the sleeve off.
Use a towel to wipe down the barbell shaft and remove all chalk and debris.
Apply 3-in-1 oil directly to the barbell shaft. Use your hands — not a towel — to work the oil in evenly. Towels absorb the oil before it can coat the bar.

REASSEMBLY — put parts back in reverse order: slide the sleeve back on. Place the thick ring. Insert the two half-moon rings into the groove. Set the thin ring inside the thick ring. Press on the first O-ring. Replace the coin. Press on the second O-ring.
Confirm the sleeve spins freely.
Repeat the full process on the other end of the barbell.
Leave the barbell flat for 24 hours in one of these locations: gun rack on the PT side, or the boneyard underneath the Gauntlet signs next to the office.
Perform this on all barbells in the maintenance area until complete.

sop_barbell_not_spinning_001.title: Barbell Not Spinning — Protocol
sop_barbell_not_spinning_001.summary: Chalk or sweat buildup is the cause. Set aside against the wall under Gauntlet signs and notify Kidd.
steps: If a barbell sleeve has stopped spinning, it means chalk or sweat has built up inside and it needs maintenance.
Set the barbell aside against the wall under the Gauntlet signs next to the office.
Notify the owner (Kidd) that it needs maintenance.
Refer to the Barbell Maintenance — Full Protocol SOP for the full procedure.

sop_tools_001.title: Tools — Location & Return
sop_tools_001.summary: All tools (screwdrivers, power drill, socket wrenches, etc.) are in the large basket on the 3rd shelf of the storage closet. Must be returned after use.
steps: Go to the storage closet.
Find the 3rd shelf.
Look for the large basket full of tools — screwdrivers, power drill, socket wrenches, and all other tools are in here.
After using any tool, return it to the basket on the 3rd shelf immediately. Do not leave tools out.

sop_massage_gun_storage_001.title: Massage Gun — Storage Protocol
sop_massage_gun_storage_001.summary: When not charging, massage gun belongs on the top right shelf of the white cubbies behind the group training wall.
steps: Whenever the massage gun is not actively charging, it must be returned to the white cubbies behind the group training wall in the recovery area.
Place it on the top right shelf.

sop_massage_gun_charging_001.title: Massage Gun — Charging Protocol
sop_massage_gun_charging_001.summary: Charge when the bottom ring turns red. Use the 8mm cord at the benches in front of the group training screen. Yellow flashing light = charging.

sop_ab_mats_001.title: Ab Mats — Storage Protocol
sop_ab_mats_001.summary: Ab mats belong in the bottom 4 cubbies of the white cubby system behind the group training wall.

sop_bike_batteries_001.title: Rogue Echo Bike — Battery Replacement
sop_bike_batteries_001.summary: Phillips head screwdriver. Access underside of screen, swap 2 AA batteries. Old batteries on 3rd shelf of supply closet for disposal. Notify Kidd or Rob if out of stock.

sop_child_dog_injury_001.title: Child or Dog Injured in the Gym — Protocol
sop_child_dog_injury_001.summary: Look for a doctor first. Ask for consent before providing first aid. Children must be in the children's area or blue chairs. Dogs must be tied to the rig next to their owner.
steps: PREVENTION — Children: children must be seated in the children's area next to the front desk or in the blue chairs by the entrance at all times. If they are elsewhere, the parent takes full responsibility.
PREVENTION — Dogs: dogs must be tied to a sturdy, floor-bolted object such as the rig, next to their owner, and away from all weights and barbells.
If an injury occurs: ask loudly if there is a doctor in the gym. Get them involved as fast as possible.
If a doctor is present: they take over. Keep the class running on the opposite side of the gym.

If no doctor is present and the injured party is a child: ask the parent for consent before touching or treating the child. If the parent says yes, provide first aid following Red Cross CPR Call-Check-Care protocol. If the parent says no, step back and do not provide care — allow the parent to handle it.
If no doctor is present and the injured party is a dog: follow the same general emergency procedure and contact the owner if they are not present.
Refer to the Acute Emergency Injury SOP if the situation escalates.

sop_toilet_001.title: Clogged Toilet — Protocol
sop_toilet_001.summary: Try plunger first (men's restroom, first stall on left). If stuck, use dish soap and hot water, place Out of Order sign, retry later. If backed up all the way, call GM immediately.
steps: Get the plunger from the men's restroom — it is in the first stall on the left.
Use the plunger to attempt to clear the clog.
If plunging clears it, you are done.
If plunging does not work: pour dish soap and hot water into the toilet. Let it sit and drain down. Place an Out of Order sign on the stall door.
Come back once it has drained and attempt to flush again. Repeat this process until cleared.
If the toilet backs up all the way: do not attempt any further fixes. Call the General Manager immediately and they will arrange for a professional to fix it.

sop_towels_001.title: Towels — Washing Protocol
sop_towels_001.summary: Coach at end of day takes towels home, washes and dries, folds, and submits a $15 invoice.
steps: The coach at the end of the day — or any available coach who has a washer and dryer — takes the towels home.
Wash them in your washing machine and dry them in your dryer.
Fold them before returning.
Submit an invoice for $15 to cover the time, transportation, and soap used.

sop_non_emergency_injury_001.title: Non-Emergency Injury — Protocol
sop_non_emergency_injury_001.summary: First aid kit in gray cabinet behind group training wall. Ask for consent. Help them make a plan for next steps. Notify owner and all coaches in Slack general channel.
steps: Examples: twisted ankle, small cut, minor scrape.
The first aid kit is in the gray heavy-duty storage cabinet behind the group training wall — same area as spray bottles and towels.
Ask the person: 'Are you okay with me helping you with first aid?' If yes, assist them using the first aid kit. If no, step back and let them handle it. Do not push.
Help them feel comfortable and cared for.
Help them make a plan for next steps — do not diagnose. Ask: 'Are you going to see your doctor or someone else about this?' Make sure they have a path forward for healing.
Notify the owner (Kidd) and all coaches in the General channel on Slack. Include what happened and where.

sop_acute_injury_001.title: Acute Emergency Injury — Protocol
sop_acute_injury_001.summary: Call for a doctor. If none, follow Red Cross Call-Check-Care. If unconscious, call 911 (5701 Almeda Rd). First aid kit in gray cubby behind group training wall. Notify Kidd when stable.
steps: Examples: barbell dropped on someone, fall from a box, anything requiring immediate medical attention.
Ask the gym loudly: 'Is there a doctor in the room?'
If a doctor is present: they take over first aid. You keep the class running on the opposite side of the gym.
If the person is unconscious and no doctor is present: have someone else call 911 immediately. Address: 5701 Almeda Road, Houston TX 77098.
Approach the person. Tap their shoulder. Say '[Name], can you hear me?' If they are unresponsive, assume consent and begin first aid. If they are responsive, ask: 'Can I provide care for you?'

If they give consent or are unresponsive: the first aid kit is a red suitcase on the gray shelf in the cubby area behind the group training wall, between the bathrooms and that wall. Additional supplies are in a clear tub surrounding the red kit. Perform first aid until first responders arrive or a more qualified person takes over.
If they do not give consent: step back and do not provide care.
If you are the one providing first aid and a class is still running: designate the most experienced athlete in the class to continue the workout on the opposite side of the gym.
Once the person is stable and first responders have been called: notify Kidd (owner) immediately. Do not call until it is safe to do so.

sop_out_of_stock_001.title: Out of Stock Items — Reporting Protocol
sop_out_of_stock_001.summary: Report in Supplies & Repairs Slack channel, notify Rob (Member Engagement Coordinator), and notify Kidd (owner).
steps: If anything in the gym is out of stock, report it immediately.

sop_rope_tape_001.title: Rope Climb Tape — Replacement Protocol
sop_rope_tape_001.summary: Must be done with another person. Ladder from supply closet, tape measure from tool drawer (3rd shelf), duct tape. Mark 10 feet and 15 feet with one rotation each.
steps: ALWAYS do this with another person present — never alone.
Get the ladder from the supply closet.
Get the tape measure from the tool drawer — 3rd shelf, tall shelving unit on the left, closest side of the supply closet.
Bring a roll of duct tape.
Set the ladder to a fully extended, stable height.
Position the ladder so the rope is DIRECTLY IN FRONT of you — never to the side. A rope to the side can push you off and topple the ladder.
Climb up to the rope that needs new tape.
Use the tape measure to find the 10-foot mark on the rope. Wrap one full rotation of duct tape at that mark.
Measure up to 15 feet. Wrap one full rotation of duct tape at that mark.
Confirm both pieces of tape are secure before coming down.
Return the ladder and all tools to the supply closet.

sop_full_clean_001.title: Full Gym Cleaning — Protocol
sop_full_clean_001.summary: Estimated 2-3 hours. Order: trash, showers, bathroom floors, toilets, restock TP and paper towels, sinks, mirrors, gym floor (blow out first then mop), equipment returns. Cleaning supplies on bottom shelf of supply closet.
steps: Estimated time: 2-3 hours to do correctly.
Cleaning supplies are on the bottom shelf or 2nd to bottom shelf of the supply closet.
STEP 1 — Empty all trash cans. Refer to the Trash Bag Replacement SOP.
STEP 2 — Clean all shower stalls. Refer to the Shower Cleaning SOP.
STEP 3 — Mop all bathroom floors. Dilute Fabuloso in the mop bucket. Wring the mop until it is just slightly damp — not soaking. Mop all bathroom floors.
STEP 4 — Scrub all toilets with Clorox wipes until they are pearl white with nothing in them but water. Flush after cleaning to prevent blue ring stains.
STEP 5 — Refill all toilet paper from the rolls in the bathroom cabinets. Refill all paper towel holders using the Torque key (refer to the Paper Towel Refill SOP).
STEP 6 — Scrub all sinks with Lysol until pearl white and completely clear.
STEP 7 — Clean all bathroom mirrors with Windex until streak-free.
STEP 8 — Blow out all dust bunnies from the gym floor first (refer to the Leaf Blower SOP), then mop the gym floor.
STEP 9 — Return all dumbbells and equipment to their correct locations. Refer to the Dumbbell Storage SOP and other storage SOPs. Do a general sweep to make sure everything is where it belongs.

sop_shower_cleaning_001.title: Shower Cleaning — Protocol
sop_shower_cleaning_001.summary: Shower cleaner spray bottle from supply closet. Spray entire shower, wipe clean — no dog hair, crumbs, or residue. Report mildew to GM.
steps: Get the shower cleaner spray bottle from the supply closet.
Ask anyone in the shower area to temporarily move their personal items.
Spray down the entire shower — walls, floor, and all surfaces.
Wipe down all sprayed surfaces.
The floor and walls should appear white and clear with no dog hair, crumbs, residue, or buildup of any kind.
If mildew or mold is forming on the drywall next to the shower: spray the affected area with the shower cleaner and scrub thoroughly until it is removed.
Report any mildew or mold to the General Manager or Kidd — even if you got it out, they need to know it is happening.

sop_leaf_blower_001.title: Leaf Blower / Gym Dust Removal — Protocol
sop_leaf_blower_001.summary: Fully charged Greenworks battery. All fans off, all doors closed. Start PT side, blow toward group side. Blow off all tops. Open garage door, blow everything out. Blow down catwalk to street.
steps: Confirm the Greenworks battery is fully charged before starting.
Turn off all fans.
Close all doors.
Start on the PT side with all doors closed. Blow all dust and dog hair toward the main group training side.
Work in left-to-right then right-to-left patterns, moving forward in small one-foot increments.
Blow dust off the top of ALL surfaces: wall balls, food/snack stand, water fountain, plate racks, dumbbells, and anything else with a flat top. Do not skip tops.
Continue the same pattern on the group training side. Work all dust toward the garage door end of the gym. Blow off tops of all equipment on this side as well.
Open the garage door. Blow all remaining dust and debris out through the garage door.
Close the garage door once all debris is outside.
Walk outside. Blow down the catwalk and ramp. Push everything all the way out to the street.

sop_floor_scrubber_troubleshoot_001.title: Floor Scrubber — Troubleshooting
sop_floor_scrubber_troubleshoot_001.summary: Excess water = clogged vacuum hose. Too much water = clogged filter. Cord yanked = reconnect black wire. Not comfortable with electronics? Call GM.
steps: If the scrubber is leaving excess water on the floor: the vacuum hose is clogged, usually from dog hair (especially if you did not blow dry the area beforehand). Remove the hose, pull out the clog, reattach the hose, lower the squeegee, and test — it should start sucking up water again.

If the scrubber is pushing out too much water: the filter may be clogged. Open the main hatch in the middle of the machine. Find the vacuum-style filter inside. Twist and remove it. Wash it in the mop sink. Allow it to fully dry before reinstalling. Return to this task once the filter is dry.

If the power cord gets yanked out: this usually means a black wire has been pulled loose from its connector. If you are comfortable working with electronics, reattach the wire and put the casing back together.
If you are NOT comfortable working with electronics: do not attempt the repair. Notify the General Manager or Kidd and they will get it fixed.

sop_floor_scrubber_operate_001.title: Floor Scrubber — Operating Protocol
sop_floor_scrubber_operate_001.summary: Always blow dry gym first. Fill front hopper with 20L water + rubber floor cleaner. Start switches left > middle > right. Hold both handles. Squeegee down. Empty dirty water into mop sink when done. Store empty.
steps: ALWAYS blow dry the gym before using the scrubber. The scrubber is not designed to pick up dog hair or debris — refer to the Leaf Blower SOP first.
Locate the front water hopper — the oval shape with a chain at the very front of the machine.
Fill it with approximately 20 liters of water. Check the water level using the clear tube with a bead on the left side near the handles.
Add a full pack of rubber floor cleaner — found on the 2nd shelf of the supply closet shelving system.
Confirm the brush is properly installed and the outer skirt around the brush is in place.

START SEQUENCE — must be done in this exact order: hit the left switch, then the middle switch, then the right switch. Hold down both handle buttons simultaneously. Confirm the squeegee at the back is DOWN.
Clean the floor in down-and-back patterns through the middle of the gym. Get inside the rigs as much as possible. Avoid black pipe equipment.
At least once per month: pull out bikes and rowers to clean behind them.

EMPTY DIRTY WATER when done: unplug the machine before emptying. Take the dirty water hose to the mop sink. Remove the hose from its bracket. Place it into the mop sink and open it to drain all dirty water. Rinse the dirty water bucket with clean water. Reattach the hose. Confirm completely empty — lean it back slightly if needed. Never leave dirty water sitting in the machine or the gym will smell.
Take the scrubber outside and empty any remaining clean water into the parking lot drain — it is just soap and water, safe to drain.
Walk it back into the supply closet. Remove the brushes and set them aside. Lift the squeegee up. Store completely empty.

sop_garage_door_policy_001.title: Garage Door — Open/Close Policy
sop_garage_door_policy_001.summary: Open only when outside temperature is between 50F and 80F. Always okay to open temporarily for cleaning.
steps: The garage door should only be opened when the outside temperature is between 50F and 80F.
If the temperature is above 80F or below 50F, keep the garage door closed.
Exception: the garage door may always be opened temporarily for cleaning purposes (blowing out dust bunnies, etc.) regardless of outside temperature.

sop_garage_door_close_001.title: Garage Door — Closing Protocol
sop_garage_door_close_001.summary: Undo chain keeper, lower door slowly hand over hand, kick both door locks in, wrap chain clockwise around both hooks with return chain in the middle.
steps: Undo the chain keeper.
Lower the door slowly hand over hand — do not let it drop or slam.
Once the door rests on the ground, kick both door locks into place on each side.
Wrap the chain back around the chain keeper in a clockwise direction.
Keep the return part of the chain in the middle.
Wrap around both hooks.

sop_garage_door_open_001.title: Garage Door — Opening Protocol
sop_garage_door_open_001.summary: Kick open both door locks, unwrap chain, pull hand over hand until fully locked at top, secure chain clockwise around both hooks with return chain in the middle.
steps: Kick open the door locks on both sides at the bottom of the door.
Unwrap the chain from its chain keeper.
Pull the chain hand over hand to raise the door.
Raise it until it reaches its full locked-out position at the top.
Secure the chain back on the chain keeper: place the return side (the side with tension) into the chain keeper first.
Run the chain through the middle of the two hooks.
Wrap clockwise over one chain link over each hook.
To close the door, refer to the Garage Door — Closing Protocol SOP.

sop_kids_class_structure_001.title: Kids Class Structure
sop_kids_class_structure_001.summary: Step-by-step class plan for when the main Kids Coach is out. Covers warm-up game, PVC deadlifts, AMRAP workout, wolf game, and handstand practice.
steps: INTRODUCTIONS: Greet every parent and let them know who you are and that you are the coach for today.

WARM-UP GAME — Flip Cone: Grab the cone stack and toss cones around the floor with some right side up and some right side down. Assign one team to get all cones right side up and the other team to get all cones right side down. Team with the most cones their way at the end wins!

PVC DEADLIFTS (5 minutes): Take out PVC sticks and spend 5 minutes working on deadlift form. Demo the movement and have the kids move along with you. Focus on improving one thing at a time. Kids will not hurt their backs using a PVC pipe. Weight is earned — if a kid demonstrates perfect form, they can earn the 15 lb silver bar.
WORKOUT — 8 Minute AMRAP: Take out boxes and set up the following workout: 5 Box Jumps, 5 Toes to Ring (as close as they can get on the low rings), 2 Wall Walks.

GAME — What's the Time Mr/Ms Wolf: One kid stands at one end of the room as the Wolf. The other kids stand at the opposite end. The group asks 'What time is it Mr/Ms Wolf?' and the Wolf calls out a time (e.g. 5 o'clock). The group takes that many steps toward the Wolf. They repeat until the Wolf yells DINNER TIME and then chases the kids. The first kid caught becomes the new Wolf. If no one is caught, the Wolf stays it.

HANDSTAND PRACTICE: Roll out the 10ft blue tumble mat and have the kids form a line far back from it. Ask each kid if they want to walk up or do a full handstand. Spot them by lightly grabbing their calf. If a kid cannot kick up yet, have them work on the kick-up and spot them through it. Your job is to help them improve and make sure no one flips over.
CLASS CLOSE: Thank the kids and lead a group closer. Count down: 1, 2, 3… CROSSFIT!!!
